tasks.commitBody:
The agenda header carried the selected collective's name and, beside it, a link to a separate /collectives page whose whole purpose was choosing from a list — a 47-line scaffold whose own comment called it provisional, whose every string was hardcoded English, and which duplicated four of its five states from branches the agenda already renders localized. The name is now the control: with two or more collectives it renders as a native select (per the #209 standing rule) that switches in place through the existing selectCollective path; with exactly one it stays plain text, unchanged; the separate page, its nav entry, its icon and its orphaned nav_collectives key are deleted, and no /collectives href remains.

The one thing the dead page did better — naming WHICH databases failed the marker check — moves into the agenda's error branch as a parameterized message in all four locales, and that branch's link becomes what it always should have been: a retry that re-runs discovery rather than a navigation.

Switching from the header is the same code path the old flow ended in: selectCollective always updated the store and re-wrote the URL in place, and every cross-collective reset on the agenda hangs off the store-value effect, not the page lifecycle — verified against each guard in the #297/#299/#325/#326/#331 family, and pinned by tests that drive the real select through single and double switches. The known unguarded path — the RSVP saved-cue reconcile documented at the savedEventIds reset, bounded by Entu event-id uniqueness — is not fixed here (its own comment rules that a separate change); the header picker is recorded on it as a third condition, per the issue's requirement that gaps be reported rather than silently inherited. The #334 offline-cache partition constraint is likewise recorded at the switch site.

Closes #338
